title: regional-queue-handoff-and-operator-runbook-2026
author: Marco Silva
body:
Purpose and scope

This runbook defines the operator playbook for regional queue handoffs and controlled traffic redistribution when a regional inference cluster is experiencing sustained capacity pressure. It covers detection triggers, safe handoff procedures (automated and manual), validation steps, common mitigations, and post-incident checks. This runbook applies to: req-router, regional-allocator, batch-orchestrator, kv-prefix-cache, and the routing layer (edge-router).

Why this matters

- Prevents prolonged tail-latency and token-cost spikes for multi-tenant customers.
- Reduces blast radius by moving only the appropriate queues/buckets rather than full-region failovers.
- Preserves tenant SLOs by executing prioritized rebalancing with minimal operator intervention.

Owner and on-call responsibilities

- Primary owner: eng-platform-ops (pager duty: eng-platform-oncall).
- Secondary owner: regional-sre.
- Runbook custodian: Marco Silva (platform scheduler team).

SLO / thresholds referenced

- Regional foreground P95 token latency: 1500ms target, 2500ms alert.
- REGION.QUEUE.BACKLOG alert: queue backlog growth > 20% for 5m AND queue length > 5k requests.
- REGION.SURGE.P50 alert: P50 latency increases > 2x baseline for 3m.
- Error budget guardrail: if region error budget burn > 15%/day, escalate to incident commander.

Detection and alert mapping

1) Automated alerts to watch:
   - grafana:REGION.QUEUE.BACKLOG
   - grafana:REGION.SURGE.P50
   - tracer:regional-allocator-evictions
   - telemetry:kv-prefix-cache-hitrate-drop

2) Initial operator checks (first 5 minutes)
   - Confirm alert on Grafana: open dashboard "Regional Queue Overview".
   - Run: curl -sS https://ops-api.internal/regions/{region}/queues | jq '.' and validate which tenant shards are hottest.
   - Check allocator: kubectl -n inference get pods | grep regional-allocator-{region} and kubectl logs for eviction spikes.
   - Confirm cloud metrics: region GPU utilization > 85% and CPU > 75% across serving nodes.

Decision tree (high level)

- If root cause is transient (traffic spike < 10m) -> prefer automated short-term evacuation (soft-handoff).
- If KV cache miss storm or cold-starts detected -> perform progressive warmup + target-prefetch.
- If sustained capacity pressure (> 30m) or node failure -> escalate to prioritized tenant redistribution and possible regional failback to multi-region routing.

Safe handoff options

1) Soft-handoff (automated, low-risk)
   - Use when backlog rises but allocator still healthy.
   - Mechanism: req-router sends a hint header X-Prefer-Alt-Region: true for low-priority tenant slices.
   - Steps (operator):
     a) Validate the hint layer is enabled: opsctl feature-get hint-routing --region {region}
     b) Trigger short-window reweight: opsctl routing adjust --region {region} --reweight-file /tmp/reweight.json --window 120s
     c) Monitor queue delta and P95 every 30s; abort if client error rate > 1.5x baseline.

2) Controlled evacuation (operator-guided)
   - Use when specific tenant shards or model variants are responsible for surge.
   - Mechanism: regional-allocator drains selected tenant slices to adjacent regions using queue affinity transfer.
   - Steps (operator):
     1) Identify candidate tenant slices via: curl -sS https://ops-api.internal/regions/{region}/hot-slices | jq '.top_slices'
     2) For each slice, run: allocatorctl move-slice --slice-id {slice} --from {region} --to {target-region} --grace-period 45s
     3) Watch: kubectl get pods -w -l slice={slice} and observe steady-state for 2x eviction intervals.
     4) Validate: KV cache warmup hitrate improves to >= 70% for moved slice within 10 minutes.

3) Emergency region redirect (high risk)
   - Use when region is degraded (node failures, network partition).
   - Mechanism: flip global routing to multi-region fallback; apply TTL-based traffic redirection to avoid cache storms.
   - Steps (operator):
     a) Open incident bridge and notify Incident Commander.
     b) Run: opsctl routing emergency-redirect --from {region} --to {target-region} --batch-size 10% --ttl 30s
     c) Incrementally increase batch-size every 2 minutes while monitoring request success rates and cost signals.

Runbook play-by-play (step checklist)

1) Triage (0-5 minutes)
   - Acknowledge alert and mark in incident tracker.
   - Capture: region, alert, top affected services, snapshots of P50/P95/P99 latencies.
   - Notify: regional-sre, platform-ops, and product-CS if customers are affected.

2) Contain (5-15 minutes)
   - Apply soft-handoff or targeted evacuation for the worst 1-3 tenant slices.
   - If manual evacuation chosen, stagger moves with 45s grace and observe eviction counts.
   - If KV cache miss storms, enable prefetch for moved slices: opsctl cache prefetch --slice {slice} --policy rolling --concurrency 4

3) Stabilize (15-60 minutes)
   - Continue incremental moves until region P95 returns to target or error budget alarm triggers.
   - If cost delta exceeds 30% vs baseline for 30 minutes, consult capacity-owner before further moves.

4) Recover and cleanup (60+ minutes)
   - If region stabilized, start reverse migration plan to return slices with warmup sequencing: move back <= 10% per 10 minutes with KV prefetching enabled.
   - Document actions in incident tracker and attach reweight JSONs and allocator logs.

Validation and observability checklist

- Dashboards to monitor: Regional Queue Overview (Grafana), KV Cache Heatmap (Grafana), Tenant Eviction Timeline (Grafana).
- Logs: regional-allocator, req-router, batch-orchestrator.
- Traces: sample traces for moved slices should show steady KV hit rates and reduced cold-starts.

Common failure modes and mitigations

- Move causes cache cold-start spike in target region -> mitigation: pause moves, enable conservative TTL pre-warming, and re-run small batch prefetch.
- Error rate for moved tenants increases -> rollback move for that slice and route traffic to intermediate fallback pool.
- Cost blowout due to cross-region token egress -> enable cost-constraint guardrail (opsctl financial hold --region {region}) and re-evaluate move plan.

Operator CLI snippets and examples

- Inspect hot slices:
  curl -sS https://ops-api.internal/regions/us-west-2/hot-slices | jq '. | {top: .[0:5]}'

- Move single slice:
  allocatorctl move-slice --slice-id slice-0421 --from us-west-2 --to us-east-1 --grace-period 45s --log-level info
\- Apply routing reweight (JSON example):
  {
    "region": "us-west-2",
    "reweights": [
      {"slice": "slice-0421", "weight": 0.5},
      {"slice": "slice-0820", "weight": 0.2}
    ]
  }

Post-incident write-up template

- Summary: one-paragraph impact and root cause.
- Timeline: bullet list with timestamps (alert, actions, stabilization).
- Actions taken: reweights, slice moves, emergency redirects.
- Metrics recovered: P95/P99 before and after, cost delta, eviction counts.
- Follow-ups: infra changes, automation opportunities (e.g., auto-slice evacuation policy), tests to add to synthetic lab.

Runbook testing and exercises

- Quarterly synthetic test: simulate a 20% traffic surge on a set of tenant slices for 30 minutes and validate soft-handoff triggers and rollback behavior.
- Monthly chaos injection: kill 1-2 serving nodes in a regional-allocator and validate operator steps for controlled evacuation.

Change history

- 2025-11-15: Created by Marco Silva.
- 2025-12-10: Added KV prefetch guidance after Q4 cache-miss incident (reviewed by Aisha Patel).
- 2026-01-22: Clarified thresholds for financial guardrail and added opsctl examples (reviewed by Lena Park).

References and related pages

Appendix: quick operator cheat sheet

- Alert acknowledged -> open incident bridge -> run hot-slices API -> decide soft-handoff vs evacuation -> execute opsctl steps -> monitor dashboards -> document and close.
